    {
      "effect_on_target": "Measures the size of both the asserted perturbation ΔA and every competing perturbation E using the Frobenius norm.",
      "id": "D001",
      "meaning": "For any natural numbers m,n and real m-by-n matrix M, defines F(M) = sqrt(Σ_{i=0}^{m−1} Σ_{j=0}^{n−1} Mᵢⱼ²). Empty sums are zero.",
      "name": "Frobenius norm",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Defines the exact attained perturbation size and the lower bound for all feasible perturbations, evaluated on the original A and b.",
      "id": "D002",
      "meaning": "For any natural numbers m,n, real m-by-n matrix A, and b ∈ ℝᵐ, defines r(A,b) = 0 if b is the zero vector, and r(A,b) = ||Aᵀb||₂ / ||b||₂ otherwise.",
      "name": "Normalized transpose residual",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Defines feasibility for ΔA and E: the zero vector must be a global least-squares minimizer for the perturbed matrix and the fixed right-hand side b.",
      "id": "D003",
      "meaning": "For any natural numbers m,n, real m-by-n matrix M, and b ∈ ℝᵐ, defines P(M,b) to mean that for every x ∈ ℝⁿ, ||b−M0||₂ ≤ ||b−Mx||₂. Since M0=0, this says ||b||₂ ≤ ||b−Mx||₂ for every x. It does not require uniqueness or zero residual.",
      "name": "Zero is a least-squares minimizer",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the vector norm in both the feasibility predicate and r(A,b) as the Euclidean norm.",
      "id": "D004",
      "meaning": "For every natural number k and vector v : Fin k → ℝ, defines ||v||₂ = sqrt(Σ_{i=0}^{k−1} vᵢ²), including value zero when k=0.",
      "name": "Euclidean vector norm",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Requires all three conclusions for the same witness ΔA: feasibility, exact norm, and the universal lower bound.",
      "id": "D005",
      "meaning": "For propositions a and b, a ∧ b asserts that both hold.",
      "name": "Logical conjunction",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Expresses exact equality of the witness norm with r(A,b), and exact equality of b with the zero vector in the definition of r.",
      "id": "D006",
      "meaning": "For any type or sort α and elements a,b of α, Eq a b is equality of those elements. Equality of vectors here means equality at every coordinate.",
      "name": "Equality",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Asserts the existence of a perturbation ΔA for each permitted m,n,A,b; it does not assert a unique perturbation or prescribe an algorithm.",
      "id": "D007",
      "meaning": "For any type or sort α and predicate p on α, ∃ a : α, p(a) asserts that some element of α satisfies p.",
      "name": "Existential quantification",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes matrices and vectors finite-dimensional with exactly m rows and n columns, permitting zero dimensions.",
      "id": "D008",
      "meaning": "For each natural number n, Fin n is the type of natural-number indices i satisfying 0 ≤ i < n.",
      "name": "Finite coordinate indices",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Interprets the addition notation in A+ΔA and A+E through the supplied matrix addition instance.",
      "id": "D009",
      "meaning": "For types α,β,γ with a specified heterogeneous addition operation, extracts that operation α × β → γ. This interface alone imposes no algebraic laws.",
      "name": "Addition operation interface",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Expresses the dimension condition n≤m, the least-squares comparison, and the perturbation lower bound using their respective order instances.",
      "id": "D010",
      "meaning": "For a type α equipped with an LE instance, extracts its binary relation ≤ on α. The interface alone imposes no order axioms.",
      "name": "Non-strict comparison interface",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Represents A, ΔA, and E as unrestricted real arrays indexed by Fin m and Fin n.",
      "id": "D011",
      "meaning": "For row-index type I, column-index type J, and entry type α, Matrix I J α is the function type I → J → α.",
      "name": "Matrices as entry functions",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Ensures that perturbations are added entrywise: (A+E)ᵢⱼ=Aᵢⱼ+Eᵢⱼ, and likewise for ΔA.",
      "id": "D012",
      "meaning": "For arbitrary row and column index types and any entry type equipped with addition, supplies matrix addition by adding corresponding entries.",
      "name": "Entrywise matrix addition",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the dimension domain, including zero, and the natural-number exponent 2 in the norm formulas.",
      "id": "D013",
      "meaning": "Nat is the type of nonnegative integers 0,1,2,….",
      "name": "Natural numbers",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "All entries, coordinates, norms, ratios, and optimization comparisons are real-valued.",
      "id": "D014",
      "meaning": "Real is the type of real numbers.",
      "name": "Real numbers",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Provides ordinary real addition in matrix perturbations and the underlying arithmetic.",
      "id": "D015",
      "meaning": "Supplies the standard addition operation on ℝ.",
      "name": "Real addition",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes residual comparisons and perturbation lower bounds comparisons in the usual real order.",
      "id": "D016",
      "meaning": "Supplies the usual non-strict order ≤ on ℝ.",
      "name": "Real order",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Connects the target's addition notation to ordinary matrix addition, and real addition where used.",
      "id": "D017",
      "meaning": "For any type α with an addition operation, supplies the heterogeneous addition interface with both inputs and output in α, using that same addition.",
      "name": "Homogeneous addition adapter",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Interprets n≤m as the usual comparison of nonnegative integer dimensions.",
      "id": "D018",
      "meaning": "Supplies the usual natural-number relation ≤.",
      "name": "Natural-number order",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Extracts real division for the ratio ||Aᵀb||₂/||b||₂.",
      "id": "D019",
      "meaning": "For any type G carrying a division-and-inversion monoid structure, extracts its division operation.",
      "name": "Division structure projection",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Provides complete finite coordinate ranges for norm sums, matrix-vector products, and the vector zero test.",
      "id": "D020",
      "meaning": "For each natural number n, supplies the finite enumeration of Fin n by 0,…,n−1, without repetition and containing every index.",
      "name": "Enumeration of finite indices",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Sums squared entries and coordinates in the Frobenius and Euclidean norm definitions.",
      "id": "D021",
      "meaning": "For any index type I, additive commutative monoid M, finite set s of indices, and function f : I → M, returns Σ_{i∈s} f(i). The empty sum is the additive identity.",
      "name": "Finite sum",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Ensures the norm sums range over every coordinate, and the finite function equality test covers every index.",
      "id": "D022",
      "meaning": "For any type α equipped with a finite enumeration, returns the finite set containing every element of α.",
      "name": "Universal finite set",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the decision for b=0 used by r(A,b), through coordinatewise equality over Fin m.",
      "id": "D023",
      "meaning": "For a finite index type α and a family of types β(a), each equipped with decidable equality, supplies decidable equality for dependent functions f,g : ∏a,β(a) by deciding whether f(a)=g(a) at every index.",
      "name": "Finite function equality decision",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Applies the real division operation in r(A,b).",
      "id": "D024",
      "meaning": "For types α,β,γ with a heterogeneous division instance, extracts its operation α × β → γ.",
      "name": "Division operation interface",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Applies real natural-number powers, specifically squares, in the norm definitions.",
      "id": "D025",
      "meaning": "For base, exponent, and result types α,β,γ with a heterogeneous power instance, extracts the exponentiation operation α × β → γ.",
      "name": "Power operation interface",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Expresses subtraction of vectors in the residuals b−M0 and b−Mx.",
      "id": "D026",
      "meaning": "For types α,β,γ with a heterogeneous subtraction instance, extracts its operation α × β → γ.",
      "name": "Subtraction operation interface",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Defines Mx in the least-squares predicate and Aᵀb in the exact perturbation-size formula.",
      "id": "D027",
      "meaning": "For any row type I, finite column type J, and coefficient type α with a non-unital, non-associative semiring structure, matrix-vector multiplication maps M : I × J → α and v : J → α to the vector with coordinate (Mv)ᵢ = Σ_{j∈J} Mᵢⱼvⱼ. Over ℝ this is ordinary matrix-vector multiplication.",
      "name": "Matrix-vector multiplication",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes the numerator in r(A,b) the Euclidean norm of the n-vector whose jth coordinate is Σ_i Aᵢⱼbᵢ.",
      "id": "D028",
      "meaning": "For any entry type and row and column index types, transpose swaps the two indices: (Mᵀ)ⱼᵢ=Mᵢⱼ.",
      "name": "Matrix transpose",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes the exponent 2 in each norm formula the usual multiplicative square.",
      "id": "D029",
      "meaning": "For any monoid M, supplies natural-number exponentiation from its monoid power operation: x⁰=1 and powers are repeated multiplication.",
      "name": "Natural powers from a monoid",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Forms part of the structure conversion supplying real arithmetic to matrix-vector multiplication, with no extra hypothesis on A or b.",
      "id": "D030",
      "meaning": "For any type with a non-unital commutative ring structure, retains the same operations and commutativity as a non-unital, non-associative commutative ring structure, forgetting the requirement of multiplicative associativity.",
      "name": "Forget multiplicative associativity requirement",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Continues the conversion of the real algebraic structure to the one required for matrix-vector products.",
      "id": "D031",
      "meaning": "For any non-unital, non-associative commutative ring, extracts its non-unital, non-associative ring structure, retaining the operations while forgetting the commutativity requirement.",
      "name": "Forget multiplicative commutativity requirement",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the addition, multiplication, and zero laws used by matrix-vector multiplication over ℝ.",
      "id": "D032",
      "meaning": "For any non-unital, non-associative ring, supplies a non-unital, non-associative semiring structure with the same addition, zero, and multiplication. It retains additive commutativity, distributivity, and zero annihilation while forgetting additive inverses as required structure.",
      "name": "Underlying semiring structure",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Extracts the algebraic operations from the real normed structure on the path to matrix-vector multiplication.",
      "id": "D033",
      "meaning": "For any non-unital normed commutative ring, supplies its underlying non-unital commutative ring, forgetting the norm and metric requirements.",
      "name": "Forget normed structure",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Starts the structure conversion from the real normed commutative ring to the algebraic structure required by matrix-vector multiplication; it does not define the vector or matrix norms in the target.",
      "id": "D034",
      "meaning": "For any normed commutative ring, supplies a non-unital normed commutative ring with the same additive operations, multiplication, norm, and metric, retaining their laws but dropping the requirement to provide a multiplicative identity.",
      "name": "Underlying non-unital normed ring",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Interprets the zero literals in the vector test and residual predicate, and the natural-number exponent 2.",
      "id": "D035",
      "meaning": "For any type α, natural number k, and specified OfNat α k instance, returns the element of α assigned to the numeral k.",
      "name": "Numeral interpretation",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes residual subtraction coordinatewise: (b−Mx)ᵢ=bᵢ−(Mx)ᵢ.",
      "id": "D036",
      "meaning": "For any index type I and family G(i) equipped with subtraction at every index, defines subtraction of dependent functions by (f−g)(i)=f(i)−g(i).",
      "name": "Pointwise function subtraction",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Defines the zero vectors in b=0 and M0 as vectors with every coordinate zero.",
      "id": "D037",
      "meaning": "For any index type I and family M(i) equipped with zero elements, defines the zero dependent function by 0(i)=0 in M(i).",
      "name": "Pointwise zero function",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supports the exact vector-zero branch in r(A,b). This logical decision instance does not itself specify a numerical algorithm for testing arbitrary real inputs.",
      "id": "D038",
      "meaning": "For every pair of real numbers a,b, supplies a decision of whether a=b, obtained from the real linear-order instance.",
      "name": "Real equality decision",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the standard real summation structure for the sums of squares.",
      "id": "D039",
      "meaning": "Equips ℝ with its usual additive commutative monoid: associative and commutative addition with identity zero.",
      "name": "Real additive commutative monoid",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the real quotient operation in r(A,b). For b≠0 the denominator ||b||₂ is positive; for b=0 the definition explicitly returns zero.",
      "id": "D040",
      "meaning": "Equips ℝ with its multiplicative monoid, inverse operation, division a/b=a·b⁻¹, and integer powers defined through natural powers and inverses. Lean's real division is total, including division by zero.",
      "name": "Real division and inversion structure",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Provides ordinary real multiplication and identity for the squares in both norm formulas and the multiplicative part of division.",
      "id": "D041",
      "meaning": "Equips ℝ with the usual multiplicative monoid: associative multiplication with identity 1.",
      "name": "Real multiplicative monoid",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies ordinary real subtraction at every coordinate of each residual.",
      "id": "D042",
      "meaning": "Defines real subtraction by a−b=a+(−b).",
      "name": "Real subtraction",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the real zero used for zero vectors and the b=0 branch of r(A,b).",
      "id": "D043",
      "meaning": "Supplies the ordinary real zero element.",
      "name": "Real zero",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the standard real algebraic operations needed for matrix-vector products through the supplied structure projections. The target's vector and matrix norms remain the explicit sums-of-squares definitions.",
      "id": "D044",
      "meaning": "Equips ℝ with its standard normed commutative ring structure: usual ring operations, absolute-value norm, usual metric, dist(a,b)=|a−b|, and the bound |ab|≤|a||b|.",
      "name": "Real normed commutative ring",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Takes the nonnegative square roots of the sums of squares in both norms. Those arguments are always nonnegative, including zero for empty sums.",
      "id": "D045",
      "meaning": "For every real x, first replaces x by its nonnegative part max(x,0), takes the nonnegative square root there, and returns it as a real number. Thus it is the usual nonnegative square root for x≥0 and equals zero for x<0.",
      "name": "Total real square root",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes zero literals denote the supplied real zero or pointwise vector zero.",
      "id": "D046",
      "meaning": "For any type α with a specified zero element, interprets the numeral 0 as that element.",
      "name": "Zero numeral adapter",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
